description:
After fz-hwn.19.2.4.9 (seal latent-activation seeding) and fz-hwn.19.2.4.12 (provider index), the semantic closure for a protocol-dispatched escaped continuation that captures a callable (e.g. defimpl Susp.run returning fn () -> f.(1) end) settles. But driving on through transport trips PR #81's guard at transport.rs generic_callable_shape: 'generic callable transport requires upstream callable surfaces for opaque or escaped demand' — the captured f's call surface (it is invoked at f.(1)) is not proven upstream in the runtime-demand callable-flow facts for this shape.

The reduce-shaped case (fz-hwn.19.2.4.9, three tests) proves surfaces and passes; this simpler direct-protocol-dispatch shape does not. Repro: compiler2_protocol_dispatched_escaped_continuation_closes_captured_callable (currently scoped to semantic closure). Fix at the runtime-demand contract that proves the captured callable's direct-call surface for an escaped continuation reached through protocol dispatch; do not compensate in transport.
title: Protocol-dispatched escaped continuation: captured callable surface not proven at transport
